To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the O(p^2) contributions to the pi pi scattering lengths are very precisely determined, 2) the O(p^{4}) and O(p^{6}) contributions have been determined with a reasonable precision (but not as precise as for the O(p^{2}) contributions), and 3) the uncertainties of the O(p^{6} contributions are larger than expected, but they have no significant impact on the total scattering length determinations.

the O(p^4) and O(p^6), low-energy couplings are well determined, that the O(p) and O(p4) contributions to the pi pi scattering lengths are well known and that the O(p6) contributions are known with a precision that is still limited, though the uncertainties are well under control.
the O(p^8) contributions to the pion-pion S-wave scattering lengths are dominated by the O(p^4) resonance contributions and that the O(p^{10}) and O(p^6)-resonance contributions are negligible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the O(p6) low-energy contributions to the pi pi scattering lengths and their impact on the final determinations.
the determination of the O(p6) contributions to pion-pion scattering lengths, and the impact of the uncertainties in the resonance masses and widths on the final results.

the determination of the scattering lengths a_0^0, a_1^1 and a_2^0, as well as the corresponding O(p^6)-contributions, from the O(p^4)- and O(p^6), low-energy couplings r_1,..., r_6, and r_{S2}, which have been estimated in a previous paper by using the hadronic inputs of the PDG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, within the uncertainties of the hadronically estimated couplings, the O(p^4) and O(p^6), as well as the total, contributions to the scattering length are consistent with the experimental data.
our results are consistent with the previous determinations of the a^0_0 and a^2_0 scattering lengths, and the O(p^2) contribution is dominant.

the present status of the O(p6) chiral expansion of the scattering lengths is satisfactory, but that a better knowledge of the O(p4) low-energy constants is needed in order to improve the precision of the results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present status of the chiral perturbation theory analysis of the pi-pi scattering lengths is satisfactory and that there is no need to go beyond the next-to-next-to-leading order for a reliable determination.

the present uncertainties of the scattering lengths are dominated by the hadronic input, while those of the O(p6) contributions to them come mostly from the uncertainties of the O(p4) low-energy constants.

, in spite of the fact that we find a good agreement with the literature for the final results, the present analysis shows that the O(p^4) chiral couplings, and in particular the ones related to the pi pi scattering lengths, are not well determined yet.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of some deviations in some individual O(p^6)-contributions, the final O(p^6)+O(p^8) results for the a^I_0 and a^I_2 scattering lengths remain sound and reliable, and the O(p^8)-contributions are still dominant.
the O(p^8) low-energy contributions should be included in the determination of the scattering lengths.
the resonance saturation approach for the O(p) couplings is a reliable method for the determination of the low-energy couplings of the chiral Lagrangian.
